feedback: Strong, honest capstone from Adebayo Aishat. On D1 you catalogued the first five findings cleanly with quoted evidence and correct classes: the SQLi string-concat line (A03/CWE-89), unsalted MD5 (A02), the alg:none verify branch returning the payload (A07), the hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (CWE-798), and the no-exp comment (CWE-613). You also nailed all three access-control issues (path traversal CWE-22, open redirect CWE-601, cookie no Secure/SameSite CWE-614) and the XXE with the SYSTEM file:///etc/passwd entity. The one real miss is finding 6: you logged a REFLECTED XSS off the login username, but the canonical bug is the STORED XSS in comments at capture 02:18:47 with the cookie beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443, which you did not cite, so that share is only partly earned. Your decoy handling in D1 is excellent and exactly right: you named the b64url helpers as the tempting-but-safe construct, proved no parser confusion or signature bypass arises from them, and correctly pointed at alg:none and the hardcoded secret as the genuine bugs. On D2 your hops are well reconciled to timestamps (SQLi 02:15:31, enumeration of 312 rows 02:16:04, file read 02:24:02) with verbatim PoC, but the chain is incomplete: you skipped the stored XSS hop 02:18:47 and the open redirect 02:21:13, so the narrative jumps. Your CVSS vectors are complete and justified, which is good, but you scored SQLi A:H when the correct value is A:N because the auth bypass does not touch availability; the file-read S:C scope change was a sharp catch. On impact you were honest to a fault: you sampled 20 rows to NGN 4,040,232 and then declined to extrapolate the remaining 292 or tie it to the BoltCash launch in roughly six weeks, where a stated-assumption estimate into the tens of millions would have earned more than a hedge. D3 is your strongest deliverable: jargon-free exec summary landing on 312 customers, a real threat model, findings tied to source files, an earliest-break fix (replace the JWT verifier to collapse the forgery path), remediation explicitly ordered by Risk Reduction per Hour of Effort rather than CVSS, and two detection stopgaps with exact fields and false-positive rates (request_body LIKE for SQLi at under 0.1 percent, jwt_header.alg='none' at near 0 percent). The flaw in D3 is that you called the XSS the disproved decoy and excluded it from scoring; the decoy is the b64url helpers, which you got right in D1, so be consistent across documents. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice, cites ISC2 Canons 1 and 4 by number, and anchors to your 312-customer finding; you cited NDPA Section 40 but framed it as the data-subject-risk duty, which is actually Section 41, while Section 40 is the 72-hour NDPC notification, so name both sections precisely. No fabrication: every figure traces to the exfil sample. The single most important fix is to treat the stored comment XSS at 02:18:47 with the beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443 as a first-class finding and weave it plus the open redirect into the exploit chain, because right now your chain and your decoy labeling both omit it.
